transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO, Pioneer Labs), Samir Patel (Platform Lead), Eve Chen (Security), Jonas (SRE)

Summary (auto): Early-stage intake for dedicated GPU reservation and isolation requirements. Focus on burst strategy and scaling expectations; security and network constraints discussed.

Topics:
- Current infra + traffic profile
- Isolation/topology options (segmented nodes vs tenant fences)
- Burst patterns: prewarm, hot-pool, and fallback routing
- SLA/latency targets and cost tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering

Action items (captured): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, quick intros — I'm Lena, AE focused on dedicated and enterprise. Ravi is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Marta Ruiz: Hi, Marta here. CTO for Pioneer Labs. Couple of folks on my side — Samir our platform lead, Eve from security, Jonas who runs SRE.
[00:16] Ravi Shah: Nice to meet you all. Quick show of hands — is the main driver cost predictability or isolation for you?
[00:22] Samir Patel: Both, honestly. We run a multimodal assistant and inference spikes when we roll out new features. We need reserved GPUs for baseline, but we want clear burst behavior.
[00:30] Marta: Right, we can't have noisy neighbors — isolation is non-negotiable for some tenant classes. Also timelines: Q3 pilot, full roll by Q4 if things look good.
[00:40] Lena: Got it. Can you share rough numbers — current RPS, tokens per request, and peak scaling factor?
[00:48] Samir: Today ~120 rps steady across our EU region, tokens ~350 per request average, peaks to ~1.8k rps during launches. That's where we saw 2–3x latency spikes.
[01:05] Jonas (SRE): And we run a central KV cache, but it's a managed memcache cluster. We worry about KV cache contention across tenants.
[01:14] Ravi: Understood — so our Dedicated offering gives you isolated GPU pools; we can set up segmented node groups for high-risk tenants and a shared warm pool for lower tiers. Prewarm strategies also help avoid cold tokenization latency.
[01:30] Marta: How deterministic is the prewarm? If we prewarm X nodes, do we guarantee the 50ms p95?
[01:38] Ravi: There's nuance — prewarm reduces cold-start variance but runtime batching and kernel selection still play. We can model expected p95 given your profile; for strict 50ms p95 we typically configure pinned low-latency instances + continuous small-batches and prefix caching. We'll need to run benchmarks to validate.
[01:58] Eve Chen: From security, we need KMS integration with our HSM, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 artifacts. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys in the private model, or do we get that in Dedicated?
[02:10] Lena: Yes — our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS; for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations too for enterprise plans. We can share our security playbook.
[02:18] Samir: And network — will Dedicated sit in our VPC or do we do a peered topology? We have strict egress rules.
[02:25] Ravi: Two patterns: a private deployment in your VPC (full control) or dedicated capacity with VPC peering and private links. The peered model still isolates data in dedicated tenant pools. We can walk through firewall port lists.
[02:38] Marta: Cost question — we want to understand unit economics for baseline reserved vs burst-on-demand. During spikes we can tolerate some higher cost, but need a predictable cap.
[02:48] Lena: We'll send a worksheet that models reserved committed GPUs vs burst minutes, with break-even points under different utilization. You can input your traffic CSV (Samir, if you share) and we'll produce expected monthly cost bands.
[03:02] Samir: We'll share a week of production traffic but also a synthetic launch pattern.
[03:08] Jonas (SRE): Another question: how do you handle fallback if Dedicated capacity saturates? Will calls fall back to hosted instances or be rejected?
[03:17] Ravi: We support policy-based routing: fail-open to a hosted model with possible higher latency and redaction of PII if policy requires, or queueing with backpressure. For strict regulatory tenants, we recommend dedicated-only with reserved buffer.
[03:30] Marta: Hmm, that fallback to hosted worries us for regulated workloads. We would want controls to prevent cross-environment routing.
[03:36] Lena: Absolutely — you can mark tenant classes as "dedicated-only". Fallbacks are configurable per-route and per-tenant. We'll document guardrails.
[03:45] Eve Chen: Ok but auditability — we need request-level logs that tie to tokens and user ids, retention controls, and ability to purge. Is that available?
[03:54] Ravi: Yes, we emit detailed traces and token-level cost breakdowns; retention is configurable on enterprise plans. Purge workflows can be provided through our support SOW.
[04:05] Marta: For benchmarking, we want to validate throughput at 500 qps sustained with p95 < 50ms for our common prompt shapes. Is that a realistic ask?
[04:14] Ravi: It's realistic if we size the pool correctly and choose the right quantization/model variant. There are tradeoffs: quantization reduces memory and cost but can add a couple milliseconds; some kernel paths perform better at longer sequence lengths. We'll propose a matrix in the benchmark plan.
[04:30] Samir: Will Redwood's runtime handle KV cache locality? We currently rely on fast local caches for prefix reuse.
[04:36] Ravi: We support KV prefix caching and sticky routing to preserve cache locality. For Dedicated we usually co-locate cache with inference nodes to reduce cross-node fetches.
[04:46] Marta: Any gotchas with model updates — if we rollout a new model how do we avoid regressions in latency or quality?
[04:53] Lena: We have rollout tools: canary, A/B, automatic fallback, and evaluation hooks. For Dedicated the rollout is controlled by you; we can run canaries in a smaller segregated pool.
[05:02] Jonas (SRE): Latency SLAs — you mentioned p95 targets earlier. Do you offer SLA credits if misses occur on Dedicated?
[05:09] Lena: For Reserved Dedicated contracts we offer SLA-backed latency and uptime with defined SLOs in the contract. We'll include typical SLA language in the SOW.
[05:16] Eve Chen: Compliance docs — send us SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, and your private deployment checklist.
[05:22] Lena: Will do.
[05:24] Marta: Timeline recap: pilot in Q3 sounds ok, but we need a short internal approval by end of April to allocate budget. So we need pricing + security docs this week.
[05:34] Lena: We'll prioritize that — Lena to send pricing + security playbook by Monday. Ravi to follow up with benchmark plan.
[05:40] Samir: On the bench plan — we'll provide representative prompt templates, token lengths, and peak windows. Can you also include recommended autoscaling headroom?
[05:48] Ravi: Yes — we'll recommend autoscaling thresholds and prewarm counts based on burst percentiles.
[05:54] Marta: One last item — are there any customers in regulated spaces using Dedicated with customer KMS?
[06:00] Lena: We have a couple of life sciences and fintech customers on Dedicated with KMS integrations and private peering. We'll share redacted references.
[06:07] Eve Chen: Great. Also question on SAML/SCIM — we need RBAC integration with our IdP.
[06:12] Ravi: Supported — enterprise SSO + SCIM provisioning. We'll show how roles map to token-level access.
[06:18] Jonas (SRE): For the benchmark harness, what's the test iam flow? Do you provision a short-lived key into our test VPC, or do you run it from Redwood side?
[06:27] Ravi: Prefer to run tests from your VPC to measure network egress and peering latency; we can provide a sample load generator and docker image. If you prefer, Redwood can also run baseline tests against a mirrored workload.
[06:39] Marta: Ok that helps. Thanks everyone.
[06:41] Lena: Quick recap of next steps — we'll send pricing worksheet, security docs, SOW template, and a proposed benchmark plan. Pioneer will share traffic CSV and select a pilot tenant class.
[06:52] Samir: We'll target sharing data by Friday.
[06:55] Lena: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the network deep-dive and benchmark kickoff.
[07:00] (call ends)
